probeMissions: BASE, common to every mission below: `node dist/cli.js init --yes --example` (runward 0.36.0, the request-triage reference mission) into an empty directory, which is green under `check --strict` (measured: exit 0). Then `node dist/cli.js check --strict --freeze` on it, which seals 18 evidence files into runward/evidence-lock.json — 11 files the manifests cite as applied evidence plus the 5 gated manifests and 2 more cited documents. That sealed tree is `m/seal`: exit 0, seal present, count 18, 0 violations. Every tampered mission is a full copy of it with exactly one thing changed. Builders kept at tools/make-missions.mjs, tools/make-freeze-missions.mjs, tools/make-extra-missions.mjs, tools/make-lock-shapes.mjs.

WRITE-SIDE missions (`check --freeze` and `check --attest`), each an unsealed copy of the base tree: f-plain, which freezes to exactly the 18-file lock, 2022 bytes, keys sorted, trailing newline present. f-bracket, which adds two house rules whose ids separate the three anchorings of `/^\[.*\]$/` — `a[b]` (contains `[`, ends with `]`, does NOT start with `[`) and `[a]b` (starts with `[`, contains `]`, does NOT end with `]`) — each `impact: LOW` so corpus divergence does not report them (an unwritten rule is only 'extra' at CRITICAL/HIGH on a gated phase), each with an `applied` row appended to the RULE CONFORMANCE table of runward/floor.md citing a file nothing else in the mission cites (code/probe-ab.ts, code/probe-ba.ts). Pristine: exit 0, `sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, both probe files in the lock. A first attempt appended the rows below the wrong table and sealed 18, which is why the row position is part of the recipe. f-unreadable was built and DISCARDED: a cited unreadable file reddens the gate with 8 EACCES conformance gaps, and `--freeze` refuses a red gate, so the write side cannot be reached that way — hence t-attest-unreadable instead.

TAMPERED (each measured on a PRISTINE tree first, so the refusal is the mission's and not a mutant's): t-file-modified (a sealed evidence file appended to after sealing) exit 1, 1 violation 'sealed evidence changed'; t-manifest-rewritten (an `applied` row in runward/floor.md rewritten to `n/a`, the RWD-2026-0008 shape) exit 1; t-manifest-touched (floor.md edited in a way that leaves everything else green, so the seal is the ONLY thing that can notice) exit 1; t-wrong-hash (one hash in the lock replaced by 64 zeros) exit 1; t-unknown-version (`version: 999`) exit 1, 'declares version 999'; t-zero-files (`files: {}`) exit 1, 'seals zero files'; t-corrupt-lock (`{ this is not json`) exit 1, 'is not valid JSON'; t-missing-file (a sealed file deleted) exit 1, 'sealed evidence missing'; t-escape-abs (`/etc/hosts` added as a lock key) and t-escape-dotdot (`../outside-secret.txt`, with that file created outside the project) both exit 1, 'sealed path escapes the project'; t-root-key (lock key `.`, which resolves EXACTLY to the project root — the only input that separates `abs === rootAbs` from `abs.startsWith(rootAbs + sep)`) exit 1, 'sealed evidence missing: .'; t-multi (version 42 + a wrong hash + an absolute key + a missing file, so all four message paths run in one process) exit 1, 4 violations; t-unreadable (a sealed, cited file chmod 000) exit 1; t-no-lock and t-lock-deleted-and-tampered (lock removed) exit 0 — the seal is opt-in, which is the control that proves the other missions' exit 1 comes from the seal.

The replacement is the visible string `"Stryker was here!"`, so if the value ever reached an artifact it would be unmissable. verdicts.argument: `files` is a Map used as an ORDERED SET: the mutated literal is the placeholder VALUE passed to `files.set(key, ...)`, and the map is read exactly once, as `[...files.keys()]`. Every value that leaves the function is recomputed from scratch on the next line — `out[rel] = sha256(join(root, rel))` — so the placeholder is overwritten before anything can observe it, and it is never even read to be overwritten. `Map.set` on an existing key also leaves that key's position unchanged, so the value cannot influence iteration order either. There is no path from this literal to the return value, to the lock, or to the attestation digest, for any mission.

verdicts.evidence: Identical measurement to the mutant above, on the second `files.set` (the sealedManifests loop). Battery: IDENTICAL on all 31 observations, both `--freeze` lock byte-comparisons and all three `--attest` digests included. Froze f-bracket under this mutant: `✓ sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, lock 2206 bytes — the same count and the same byte length as pristine, no 'Stryker' anywhere in the 20 rows.
verdicts.argument: Same construction, same argument: the literal is the placeholder value of a Map whose only read is `[...files.keys()]`, and every emitted hash is recomputed by `out[rel] = sha256(join(root, rel))`. This call site additionally re-sets keys the first loop may already have inserted (a gated manifest that is also cited evidence), and `Map.set` on an existing key changes neither the position nor anything a reader can see, since the value is never read. No mission can distinguish a value that nothing consumes.

verdicts.evidence: Battery: observable on 2 (freeze:f-plain, freeze:f-bracket), and on nothing else — notably NOT on the three `--attest` runs, because missionStateDigest re-sorts the keys before hashing. Close-up (tools/one.mjs `--mode freeze --mission f-plain`): the same 18 files with the same 18 hashes, written in TRAVERSAL order instead of sorted order — the lock now begins `code/src/core/ports/model-provider.port.ts`, `code/src/core/application/triage-request.usecase.ts`, `code/src/adapters/keyword-model.adapter.ts`, … with `AGENTS.md` in thirteenth position and the five gated manifests pushed to the end, where pristine writes `AGENTS.md` first and the manifests in alphabetical position. tools/order-downstream.mjs confirms the scope of the harm: a lock written by this mutant still REFUSES a file modified after sealing (exit 1, 1 violation), so this is artifact corruption, not a false green — the function's contract, stated in its own docstring as 'stable order, byte-idempotent on unchanged evidence', is what breaks. Nothing in the suite reddens; a lock file committed to a repository churns on every re-freeze.
